references.text: Israel abandoned the Lord and served Baal and the images of Ashtoreth, illustrating the pattern of turning away from foreign gods.
Samuel urged Israel to remove the foreign gods and the images of Ashtoreth and serve only the Lord, which they did.
Jacob commanded his household to remove the foreign gods from among them, an early example of cleansing oneself from idolatry.
Joshua challenged Israel to remove the foreign gods and serve the Lord, and the people promised to serve him.
The Lord shared in the suffering of His people in all their distress, expressing God's compassion for Israel's affliction.
God's heart was moved within Him, and His compassion was stirred, showing God's deep feelings toward Israel.
The Lord saw the suffering of Israel in Egypt and could no longer hold back, demonstrating His compassion for the people's distress.
God remembered His covenant and relented according to His great mercy, describing how God responded to Israel's repentance.
